name: Creatine water retention concerns
lead: Creatine water retention concerns refers to worries in looksmaxxing communities that creatine supplements cause facial bloating or puffiness. Reference sources describe early weight gain from creatine as water moving into muscle, mainly during loading.[1]
Long-term studies are described as suggesting creatine does not necessarily change total body water relative to muscle mass.[1] No studies were found specifically on creatine and facial appearance.

paras: In a looksmax.org thread, one user asked whether creatine bloats the face; one reply said creatine and minoxidil bloated their face, while another reported no bloating using both.[2]

Early weight gain on creatine is attributed to osmotic water movement into muscle.[1] A 2009 systematic review found no good evidence that creatine impairs hydration or heat tolerance.[1] A 2019 National Kidney Foundation review found creatinine slightly raised but within normal limits.[1]
No studies found on creatine and facial bloating. Studies on body water are summarised in general references.[1]

timeline.event: Strength-oriented creatine supplements reach the market.[1]

lore.intro: Users on looksmax.org discuss whether creatine puffs the face, with mixed anecdotes.[2]

claims.believers: Some users say creatine made their face look bloated.[2]
claims.experts: Reviews attribute early weight gain to water in muscle, and no studies of facial effects were found.[1]

card.summary: Whether creatine puffs the face; water goes into muscle per reviews, facial effects untested.

quick.overview:
Some users worry creatine bloats the face.

References describe water entering muscle; no studies address the face.
quick.mechanism: Creatine raises muscle creatine and draws water in by osmosis.
quick.risks: Reviews report no kidney harm in studied groups; safety data are lacking for children and pregnancy.
